questions.stem: A service's build runs `javac -cp 'libs/*' -d out src/**/*.java`. One jar in `libs` holds a processor, registered in its `META-INF/services/javax.annotation.processing.Processor`, that writes the `Metrics_` classes the service's code calls. The team moves the build from JDK 21 to JDK 25 and changes nothing else. What does the first compile on JDK 25 do?

options.text: It compiles the `Metrics_` callers and prints nothing about processing, since a services file registers the processor with every compile that sees the jar
options.says: javac 25 ran no processor found only on the class path, and the compile failed

options.text: It fails at the `Metrics_` callers with `cannot find symbol`, since javac 25 runs no processor it finds only on the class path
options.says: javac 21 ran it with a note that a future release may not; javac 25 didn't, and the compile failed with cannot find symbol

options.text: It compiles the `Metrics_` callers and prints a note about a future change to discovery, since javac 25 still runs processors it finds on the class path
options.says: the note is javac 21's; javac 25 no longer runs the processor

options.text: It fails before the `Metrics_` callers with `cannot access` for the processor class, since javac 25 refuses to load a processor from the class path
options.says: javac 25 didn't mention the processor: it ran none, and the error was cannot find symbol in the code that uses the generated class

origin.section: A Processor Is Code javac Runs During the Compile, and What It Adds Is New Source Files

questions.stem: A processor checks that every `@Scheduled` method takes no parameters. For a method that does, it runs `processingEnv.getMessager().printMessage(Diagnostic.Kind.ERROR, "@Scheduled method must take no parameters")` and carries on with the next method. A module of 600 classes has one such method. What does its compile show?

options.text: An error on the method's line and a failed build, since javac takes the location from the element `process` is handling when the call runs
options.says: javac takes a location only from an element passed to printMessage; without one it printed no file and no line

options.text: A warning with no file or line and a passing build, since javac turns an error that the call gives no place into a warning
options.says: the kind decides: an ERROR without an element is still an error and fails the compile

options.text: A warning on the method's line and a passing build, since javac places the call's message at the method being checked and only an exception fails a build
options.says: an ERROR message fails the compile, and without an element it has no location

options.text: An error with no file or line and a failed build, since javac reports the error and the call gives it no place to report it at
options.says: without an element javac printed `error:` and the message with no location, and the compile failed

origin.section: An Error Reported at the Element Makes javac Point at the User's Line

questions.stem: A processor adds the number of `@Entity` classes each call of `process` sees to an `int` field, and writes `EntityCount.java` with that number when `processingOver()` is true. The sources have three `@Entity` classes, and another processor in the same compile generates two more from them. How many calls of `process` does this processor get, and what number does it write?

options.text: Two calls, writing 5, since a processor is called only in rounds that bring its annotation, and one object counts both
options.says: a processor called in one round is called in every later round, including the last, where processingOver() is true: three calls

options.text: Three calls, writing 0, since javac makes a new processor object for each round, and the last one has seen nothing
options.says: javac creates the processor object once per compile, so its fields carry over between rounds

options.text: Three calls, writing 5, since a processor is called in every round after its first, and one object counts across them
options.says: round 1 has the sources, round 2 the generated classes, round 3 nothing and processingOver() true; one object sees all three

options.text: Two calls, writing 0, since javac makes a new processor object for the last call, and that call sees no classes
options.says: there are three calls, all on one processor object, so the field holds 5 when processingOver() is true

origin.section: Processing Runs in Rounds, and a Generated File Is Processed in the Next One

questions.stem: A team wants a `toJson()` for every class marked `@Json`, generated by an annotation processor that uses no compiler internals. Which approach works?

options.text: Write a new `<Name>Json.java` with a static `toJson(<Name>)`, since the `Filer` writes it as a class of its own beside `<Name>`
options.says: a processor adds new files; code that wants the generated behaviour calls the generated class

options.text: Write a new `<Name>Json.java` with an instance `toJson()`, since the `Filer` writes it as a class of its own that javac adds to `<Name>`'s supertypes
options.says: a generated class is a class of its own; javac adds nothing to the supertypes of a class the sources declare, which would have to extend it themselves

options.text: Write `<Name>.java` again with a static `toJson(<Name>)` added, since the `Filer` replaces the file of a type the sources declare
options.says: creating a file for a type in the sources throws FilerException: Attempt to recreate a file for type

options.text: Write `<Name>.java` again with an instance `toJson()` added, since a file generated under the class's name takes its place
options.says: creating a file for a type in the sources throws FilerException; the initial inputs count as created by a zeroth round

origin.section: The Filer Creates Each File Once and Never Replaces a Class That Exists
